evidence: src/application/task-management-service.ts: `private readonly users = new Map<string, User>()`, `projects = new Map<string, Project>()`, `tasks = new Map<string, Task>()` act as the data store, which is infrastructure (repository) work.
src/application/task-management-service.ts: `nextUserId`, `nextProjectId`, `nextTaskId` counters and `String(this.nextTaskId++)` create IDs the way a database would, which is infrastructure work.
src/application/task-management-service.ts: `getUser`, `getProject`, `getTask` look records up directly in the Maps, which is repository (infrastructure) work.
src/application/task-management-service.ts: `markTaskDone` enforces the rule that a done task cannot be marked done again, which is a domain-entity rule.

parsedVerdict.reasoning: TaskManagementService is in the application layer. Coordinating use cases is the right job for it. The problem is that the class also stores and looks up the data itself. It keeps all users, projects and tasks in its own in-memory Maps, creates their IDs from counters, and fetches records by ID. That is repository (persistence) work, which belongs in the infrastructure layer, normally behind a repository interface. The file also holds domain rules: required-text checks, valid-status checks, due-date checks, and the rule that a task already marked done cannot be marked done again. Domain entities should enforce these. Finally, it attaches HTTP status codes (404, 409) to the errors it throws, which is a transport concern. The persistence work alone is enough to fail the rubric.

violations.message: The class stores and looks up data itself. Its in-memory Maps (users, projects, tasks), ID counters (nextUserId, nextProjectId, nextTaskId) and lookups (getUser, getProject, getTask) are persistence work. That belongs in the infrastructure layer behind a repository interface.

markTaskDone enforces the rule that a done task cannot be marked done again, and requireStatus, requireText and validateDueDate check entity validity. These are domain rules and belong on the domain entities, not in the application service.
DomainError is thrown with HTTP status codes 404 and 409 in getUser, getProject, getTask and markTaskDone. Mapping errors to HTTP status codes is a transport (infrastructure) concern.
